title: G-equivariant sheaves and cosheaves
body_html:
$G$-equivariant sheaves and cosheaves

Assume $G$ acts cellularly on $X$ (see Locally finite regular CW complex with cellular G-action).

Definition. A $G$-equivariant $\mathscr{C}$-valued sheaf on $X$ is a pair $(V,a)$ where $V$ is a sheaf on $X$ and $a$ assigns to each $g \in G$ a morphism $a(g) \in \Hom(V, g^*V)$ satisfying $a(gh) = (h^* a(g)) \circ a(h)$, with $g^*V$ obtained by post-composing $V$ with $g : ]X[ \to ]X[$.

Cellular form. Equivalently, a $G$-equivariant sheaf is a collection

  • $V_F$, one object of $\mathscr{C}$ for each cell $F \in [\![X]\!]$;
  • a restriction $r^V_{E,F} : V_E \to V_F$ for each $E \preceq F$;
  • an isomorphism $a^V_{g,F} : V_F \to V_{gF}$ for each $g \in G$, $F \in [\![X]\!]$,

subject to four compatibilities:

  • $r^V_{E,E} = \id_{V_E}$;
  • $r^V_{E,F} \circ r^V_{D,E} = r^V_{D,F}$ for $D \preceq E \preceq F$;
  • $a^V_{g,hF} \circ a^V_{h,F} = a^V_{gh,F}$;
  • $a^V_{g,F} \circ r^V_{E,F} = r^V_{gE,gF} \circ a^V_{g,E}$ (equivariance of restrictions).

A $G$-equivariant cosheaf has the analogous data with restriction directions reversed.

Notation. We write $\Sh_G(X,R)$ (resp.\ $\Cosh_G(X,R)$) for $G$-equivariant $R$-modules; for the trivial group we recover $\Sh(X,R) = \Sh_{\{e\}}(X,R)$.

Lean formalization

Naming convention: functor form (Sheaf, Cosheaf) vs object form (Sheaf', Cosheaf')

Two equivalent presentations of the underlying (non-equivariant) (co)sheaf exist in the paper, and the Lean library encodes both under distinct names:

  • Sheaf X C, Cosheaf X C (no prime) — functor form. Literal X ⥤ C and Xᵒᵖ ⥤ C, introduced as abbrevs. All of Mathlib's CategoryTheory.Functor API applies directly with no wrapping. This is the canonical form used throughout the library — GEquivariantSheaf, GEquivariantCosheaf, GCosheaf, GCosheaf.toFunctor, and the reduction chain (Reduction of G-equivariant cosheaves to a QFD) all sit on top of it.

  • Sheaf' X C, Cosheaf' X C (with prime) — object form. Sheaf7 §2.2's classical $(V, r)$-pair form as a structure with fields obj : X → C and (co)restriction morphisms map : E ≤ E' → … plus functoriality axioms. Kept as a concrete surface for constructions that read more clearly with explicit field access than with functor destructuring.

The two forms are provably equivalent via Sheaf.toObject, Sheaf.ofObject, Cosheaf.toObject, Cosheaf.ofObject (all four in SheafOnBuilding.SheafCosheaf). Downstream code should PREFER the no-prime (functor) form — it composes with Mathlib's functor-category API for free; the primed form exists to bridge the paper's presentation for readers whose mental model is object-oriented.

Equivariance data

The class GEquivariantCosheaf G X F (typeclass on a single cosheaf F) records the pointwise action data

act : ∀ (g : G) (E : X), F.obj (op E) ≅ F.obj (op (g • E))

as a family of isomorphisms (matching the paper's convention "$g_* : V_E \xrightarrow{\sim} V_{gE}$"), together with three axioms — act_map (naturality with cosheaf restrictions), act_one (identity of $G$ acts as $\mathbf 1$ modulo eqToHom for $1 \cdot E = E$), and act_mul (multiplicativity modulo eqToHom for $(g\cdot h)\cdot E = g\cdot(h\cdot E)$).

Why Iso and not just a morphism. For a Group G invertibility of act g follows abstractly, but packaging as Iso from the start gives downstream code direct access to .inv, avoiding rewrite-motive typechecking failures on rw [inv_one] when g⁻¹ appears in an eqToHom target type. The derived lemma GEquivariantCosheaf.act_one_inv records that (act 1 E).inv equals the eqToHom bridging W_{1 \cdot E} = W_E.

For §2.7 (Prop 2.7.2) we need $\Cosh_G(X, C)$ as a category (not just a predicate on individual cosheaves): the file GCosheaf.lean supplies the bundled type GCosheaf G X C := (base : Cosheaf X C, equiv : GEquivariantCosheaf G X base) together with a Category instance whose morphisms are natural transformations of the underlying cosheaves commuting with act g E at every cell. See The transporter categories ]X/G[ and [X/G] for the ]X/G[-side of the same story.

lean_refs.name: SheafOnBuilding.Sheaf
lean_refs.signature: abbrev Sheaf (C : Type*) [Category C] : Type _ := X ⥤ C

lean_refs.name: SheafOnBuilding.Cosheaf
lean_refs.signature: abbrev Cosheaf (C : Type*) [Category C] : Type _ := Xᵒᵖ ⥤ C

lean_refs.name: SheafOnBuilding.Sheaf'
lean_refs.signature:
structure Sheaf' (C : Type*) [Category C] where
  /-- Object at each cell. -/
  obj : X → C
  /-- Restriction morphism for a face relation. -/
  map : ∀ {E E' : X}, E ≤ E' → (obj E ⟶ obj E')
  /-- Restriction along the identity face is the identity morphism. -/
  map_id : ∀ E, map (le_refl E) = 𝟙 (obj E) := by aesop_cat
  /-- Restriction is compatible with composition of face relations. -/
  map_comp : ∀ {E E' E'' : X} (h : E ≤ E') (h' : E' ≤ E''),
    map (le_trans h h') = map h ≫ map h' := by aesop_cat

lean_refs.name: SheafOnBuilding.Cosheaf'
lean_refs.signature:
structure Cosheaf' (C : Type*) [Category C] where
  /-- Object at each cell. -/
  obj : X → C
  /-- Corestriction morphism for a face relation (note the reversed
  arrow direction compared to `Sheaf'`). -/
  map : ∀ {E E' : X}, E ≤ E' → (obj E' ⟶ obj E)
  /-- Corestriction along the identity face is the identity morphism. -/
  map_id : ∀ E, map (le_refl E) = 𝟙 (obj E) := by aesop_cat
  /-- Corestriction is compatible with composition of face relations. -/
  map_comp : ∀ {E E' E'' : X} (h : E ≤ E') (h' : E' ≤ E''),
    map (le_trans h h') = map h' ≫ map h := by aesop_cat

lean_refs.name: SheafOnBuilding.Sheaf.toObject
lean_refs.signature:
def toObject {C : Type*} [Category C] (F : Sheaf X C) : Sheaf' X C where
  obj := F.obj
  map h := F.map (homOfLE h)
  map_id E := F.map_id E
  map_comp _ _ := F.map_comp _ _

lean_refs.name: SheafOnBuilding.Sheaf.ofObject
lean_refs.signature:
def ofObject {C : Type*} [Category C] (F : Sheaf' X C) : Sheaf X C where
  obj := F.obj
  map {_ _} h := F.map (leOfHom h)
  map_id := F.map_id
  map_comp _ _ := F.map_comp _ _

lean_refs.name: SheafOnBuilding.Cosheaf.toObject
lean_refs.signature:
def toObject {C : Type*} [Category C] (F : Cosheaf X C) : Cosheaf' X C where
  obj E := F.obj (op E)
  map h := F.map (homOfLE h).op
  map_id E := F.map_id (op E)
  map_comp _ _ := F.map_comp _ _

lean_refs.name: SheafOnBuilding.Cosheaf.ofObject
lean_refs.signature:
def ofObject {C : Type*} [Category C] (F : Cosheaf' X C) : Cosheaf X C where
  obj E := F.obj E.unop
  map {_ _} h := F.map (leOfHom h.unop)
  map_id _ := F.map_id _
  map_comp _ _ := F.map_comp _ _

lean_refs.name: SheafOnBuilding.GEquivariantSheaf
lean_refs.signature:
class GEquivariantSheaf {C : Type*} [Category C] (F : Sheaf X C) where
  /-- Stalk-level action of `g` at `E` as an iso. -/
  act : ∀ (g : G) (E : X), F.obj E ≅ F.obj (g • E)
  /-- Naturality against sheaf restrictions. -/
  act_map : ∀ (g : G) {E F' : X} (h : E ≤ F'),
    (act g E).hom ≫ F.map (homOfLE (GCellComplex.smul_le g h)) =
      F.map (homOfLE h) ≫ (act g F').hom
  /-- Identity: `act 1 E = 𝟙`, modulo `eqToHom` for `1 • E = E`. -/
  act_one : ∀ E : X,
    (act 1 E).hom ≫ eqToHom (show F.obj ((1 : G) • E) = F.obj E by rw [one_smul]) =
      𝟙 (F.obj E)
  /-- Multiplicativity. -/
  act_mul : ∀ (g h : G) (E : X),
    (act (g * h) E).hom ≫
        eqToHom (show F.obj ((g * h) • E) = F.obj (g • h • E) by rw [mul_smul]) =
      (act h E).hom ≫ (act g (h • E)).hom

lean_refs.name: SheafOnBuilding.GEquivariantCosheaf
lean_refs.signature:
class GEquivariantCosheaf {C : Type*} [Category C] (F : Cosheaf X C) where
  /-- Stalk-level action of `g` at `E` as an iso. -/
  act : ∀ (g : G) (E : X), F.obj (op E) ≅ F.obj (op (g • E))
  /-- Naturality against cosheaf restrictions: for `h : E ≤ F'`,
  ```
  F.obj (op F') ──── F.map (homOfLE h).op ──► F.obj (op E)
       │                                          │
       │ (act g F').hom                           │ (act g E).hom
       ▼                                          ▼
  F.obj (op (g•F')) ─ F.map (...smul_le...).op ► F.obj (op (g•E))
  ```
  -/
  act_map : ∀ (g : G) {E F' : X} (h : E ≤ F'),
    F.map (homOfLE h).op ≫ (act g E).hom =
      (act g F').hom ≫ F.map (homOfLE (GCellComplex.smul_le g h)).op
  /-- Identity: `(act 1 E).hom = 𝟙`, modulo `eqToHom` for `1 • E = E`. -/
  act_one : ∀ E : X,
    (act 1 E).hom ≫
        eqToHom (show F.obj (op ((1 : G) • E)) = F.obj (op E) by rw [one_smul]) =
      𝟙 (F.obj (op E))
  /-- Multiplicativity. -/
  act_mul : ∀ (g h : G) (E : X),
    (act (g * h) E).hom ≫
        eqToHom (show F.obj (op ((g * h) • E)) = F.obj (op (g • h • E))
          by rw [mul_smul]) =
      (act h E).hom ≫ (act g (h • E)).hom

lean_refs.name: SheafOnBuilding.GEquivariantCosheaf.act_one_inv
lean_refs.signature:
theorem act_one_inv (E : X) :
    (act (G := G) (1 : G) E).inv =
      eqToHom (show F.obj (op ((1 : G) • E)) = F.obj (op E) by rw [one_smul])

lean_refs.name: SheafOnBuilding.smulFunctor
lean_refs.signature:
def smulFunctor (g : G) : X ⥤ X where
  obj E := g • E
  map h := homOfLE (GCellComplex.smul_le g (leOfHom h))

lean_refs.name: SheafOnBuilding.GCosheaf
lean_refs.signature:
structure GCosheaf (C : Type*) [Category C] where
  /-- Underlying cosheaf `F : Xᵒᵖ ⥤ C`. -/
  base : Cosheaf X C
  /-- The equivariant structure witnessing `G`-equivariance. -/
  equiv : GEquivariantCosheaf G X base
lean_refs.docstring: Bundled `G`-equivariant cosheaf on `X` with values in `C`.

lean_refs.name: SheafOnBuilding.GCosheaf.category
lean_refs.signature:
instance category : Category (GCosheaf G X C) where
  Hom F F' := Hom F F'
  id F := Hom.id F
  comp α β := Hom.comp α β
  id_comp _ := Subtype.ext (Category.id_comp _)
  comp_id _ := Subtype.ext (Category.comp_id _)
  assoc _ _ _ := Subtype.ext (Category.assoc _ _ _)
